run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-16T23:11:29Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The frontend RequestErrorRate alert is firing because frontend's calls to product-catalog fail: the Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog was rolled out at 23:09:38 with container command ["invalid-command"], so its only pod cannot start (StartError, exitCode 128, CrashLoopBackOff) and the product-catalog Service has no ready endpoints. Frontend error spans went from 0 to roughly 17-23 error spans/s (5m rate) starting in the 23:11 bucket; at 23:20:29 the 5m error-span rate was 17.68/s (alert annotation says 16.87), and the errors sit on exactly the frontend operations that call ProductCatalogService/GetProduct, plus the API routes and page spans that depend on it. Recommendation and checkout also produced their own error spans on calls to ProductCatalogService, and frontend-proxy produced ingress/router error spans on the same traffic. All flagd fault flags are off and no NetworkPolicies exist, so runtime flag injection and network misconfiguration were considered and rejected; the observed fault path is the container command in the Deployment pod template.

claims.text: Frontend error spans (traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}) were 0 in every returned 5m-rate point from 22:56:01 through the 23:06:01 bucket, then rose from 1.72/s in the 23:11:01 bucket to a peak of about 23.2/s, and were 17.68/s at 23:20:29 with 13.00/s UNSET at the same instant.

Within frontend, the error spans are on GET (about 5.1/s), GET /api/products/{productId} and executing api route (pages) /api/products/[productId] (about 4.3/s each), GET /api/recommendations and executing api route (pages) /api/recommendations (about 0.81/s), POST /api/checkout and executing api route (pages) /api/checkout and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (about 0.51/s), grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct (about 4.3/s), grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations (about 0.81/s) and tcp.connect (about 0.015/s); GET /api/cart, POST /api/cart, GET /api/data and the cart/ad client spans show 0 error rate.

The Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog pod template runs image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog with command ["invalid-command"], and the Deployment reports unavailableReplicas 1 with condition Available=False (MinimumReplicasUnavailable) since 2026-11-16T23:09:55Z.

Pod product-catalog-fcf7564cf-vjj7l (owner ReplicaSet product-catalog-fcf7564cf, startTime 2026-11-16T23:09:55Z) is Running but not ready, restartCount 5, container state waiting reason CrashLoopBackOff ("back-off 2m40s restarting failed container=product-catalog"), and lastState terminated reason StartError exitCode 128 with message: failed to create containerd task ... exec: "invalid-command": executable file not found in $PATH (finishedAt 2026-11-16T23:13:08Z).

Kubernetes events for Deployment product-catalog show ScalingReplicaSet scaling up product-catalog-fcf7564cf from 0 to 1 at 23:09:38Z and again at 23:09:55Z and scaling down the previous ReplicaSet product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc from 1 to 0 at 23:09:47Z; ReplicaSet product-catalog-fcf7564cf created pods at 23:09:38Z and 23:09:55Z, and its pods recorded repeated Warning Failed events (6 on pod vjj7l) carrying the same exec "invalid-command" error plus 25 Warning BackOff events between 23:10:00Z and 23:15:10Z.

ReplicaSet product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc (created 22:39:37Z, owner Deployment product-catalog, replicas 0) has no container command, while the newer ReplicaSet product-catalog-fcf7564cf (created 23:09:38Z, same owner, replicas 1) carries command ["invalid-command"] on the same image, i.e. a configuration-only change produced the new ReplicaSet.

Among all 21 Deployments in namespace otel-demo, product-catalog is the only one whose container specifies a command value of ["invalid-command"]; every other application container has command and args null (flagd runs /flagd-build start ... and otel-collector passes --config).

Product-catalog span volume stopped: traces_span_metrics_calls_total for service_name=product-catalog ran about 13.5/s at the 23:12:01 bucket, 3.21/s at 23:14:01 and 0 at 23:16:01, 23:18:01 and 23:20:01, while frontend (41-56/s) and recommendation (about 2.7-3.2/s) kept emitting spans over the same period.

The Service endpoints object for product-catalog contains only notReadyAddresses (pod product-catalog-fcf7564cf-vjj7l, ip 100.96.2.148) and no ready addresses, while frontend, frontend-proxy, checkout and recommendation endpoints have ready addresses.

Recommendation, checkout and frontend-proxy each produced their own error spans in the window: recommendation error rate was 0 until the 23:13:01 bucket then rose to about 0.93-2.07/s on /oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts and get_product_list; checkout was 0 until 23:13:01 then about 0.58-1.32/s on oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct; frontend-proxy ingress and router frontend egress error rate rose from about 2.68/s in the 23:11:01 bucket to about 14.1/s peak.

Accounting (orders receive), ad (flagd EventStream/ResolveBoolean), fraud-detection and payment returned error-span rates of 0 except ad flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream at about 0.004/s throughout the window, far below the incident signal and not on product-catalog call paths.

Jaeger traces returned for frontend span the period around 22:54:56Z only (source_start_at 2026-11-16T22:54:56.572092Z, source_end_at 22:54:56.881952Z); those sampled traces show frontend GET /api/products/{productId}, grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct, frontend-proxy ingress, cart calls and load-generator spans all with http.status_code=200 / rpc.grpc.status_code=0, i.e. the sampled trace view predates the failure and contains no error spans.

No NetworkPolicy objects exist in namespace otel-demo (the query returned an empty list), and the product-catalog Service exists with port tcp-service 8080; its lack of ready addresses matches a not-ready pod rather than a network or Service-configuration block.

The flagd-config ConfigMap lists the fault-injection flags adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure and recommendationCacheFailure; every one has defaultVariant "off" (state ENABLED).

A runtime fault-injection flag (for example flagd productCatalogFailure) causing frontend errors is rejected: that flag and all other demo flags have defaultVariant "off", and the observed product-catalog failure is a container-start exec error, which a runtime feature flag cannot produce.

A NetworkPolicy or Service-routing problem between frontend and product-catalog is rejected: no NetworkPolicies exist in otel-demo and the product-catalog Service already had a target pod, which was listed only as notReady because its container never started.

Resource exhaustion (OOMKilled) on product-catalog is rejected: the container's last termination reason is StartError with exitCode 128 and the exec error message, not OOMKilled, and no Evicted event or OOM termination appears among the product-catalog pod events.

The single fault setting that matches the observed failure path is the Deployment otel-demo/product-catalog pod template's container command ["invalid-command"]: it makes the only replica fail at container init, leaves the Service with no ready endpoint from 23:09:47Z onward, and the frontend/recommendation/checkout error spans are on the operations that call ProductCatalogService; the object that applied this change (Deployment product-catalog) is therefore the origin of the incident.

Advisory: restore the product-catalog Deployment pod template to a valid container entrypoint (for example roll back to the revision served by ReplicaSet product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc) rather than only deleting the pod, then confirm one product-catalog replica becomes Ready and the Service gains a ready endpoint before validating that frontend error spans return to 0.

gaps: No change_history integration is available in this Run, so what or who changed the product-catalog Deployment pod template command to ["invalid-command"] at ~23:09:38Z could not be verified.

Jaeger returned no traces for frontend inside 23:12:00-23:21:01 and the sampled frontend traces it did return stop at 22:54:56Z, so the incident-window gRPC/HTTP status detail of the failing calls (for example grpc status Unavailable) is unknown; a product-catalog trace search for the same window was refused as RESULT_TOO_LARGE (evidence_id 04bb81e6-fc4f-4965-a9a4-73fe3137c3da-t1:aa75cc97-2308-4791-a123-180791aa07bf, not citable) and was not needed for the conclusion.
product-catalog container logs are empty because the container never started, and the filtered frontend log read returned no lines, so the exact frontend-side error text was not observed.

The listed metrics rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count, rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket and http_server_request_duration_seconds_count returned no series for frontend in the query window, so no latency baseline and no HTTP/gRPC status-code breakdown could be produced.

No ERROR-status span series was returned for cart, currency, email, image-provider, quote, shipping, kafka or load-generator, which is unknown rather than proof that they stayed healthy; those services were not otherwise checked.

Prometheus has no rule named RequestErrorRate, so the alerting rule's exact expression and evaluation could not be verified; the alert's own current value of 16.87 was compared only against the measured 5m error-span rate of 17.68/s at 23:20:29.

Pod and ReplicaSet objects reflect the cluster state at query time, so the pre-23:09 deployment revision is inferred from ReplicaSet product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc's spec and the rollout events, not from a stored revision history.
next_steps: Revert the otel-demo/product-catalog Deployment container command to its pre-23:09:38Z value (e.g. kubectl rollout undo deployment/product-catalog) so the pod can start, instead of deleting the crashing pod.

After the rollback, confirm kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready for otel-demo/product-catalog returns to 1, the product-catalog Service endpoints gain a ready address, and frontend STATUS_CODE_ERROR span rate returns to 0.

Add a guard (admission policy or manifest validation) that rejects container command values that do not exist in the image, and restrict who can patch the product-catalog Deployment pod template, since this change took the service fully unavailable within about 90 seconds.
Enable change-history/audit visibility for the cluster so the actor and exact patch behind the 23:09:38Z product-catalog rollout can be identified.
